answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the forge check immediately, the wander audit keeps the resolved set and the spiral replay makes public exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 67 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 67 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 5 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
